newsitem.title: USA: Invacare hits Georgia anti-takeover bill.
newsitem.headline: Invacare hits Georgia anti-takeover bill.

text.p: Invacare Corp on Friday criticized an anti-takeover bill introduced in the Georgia legislature, saying it suspected Healthdyne Technologies Inc was behind the bill.
Invacare has launched a hotile takeover bid for Healthdyne, which is based in Marietta, Ga. Healthdyne has rejected the $13-a-share offer.
"We strongly suspect that the board and management of Healthdyne...are behind this (legislative) proposal," said A. Malachi Mixon III, Invacare chairman and chief executive officer.
Mixon said Healthdyne would most obviously benefit from the bill, which was introduced in the legislature yesterday.
The bill would alter the way publicly held Georgia corporations elect board members, instituting a so-called staggered scheme. Only one-third of a board would stand for election each year.
"Without this bill, Healthdyne's entire board must stand for re-election at the upcoming 1997 annual meeting," Mixon said.
If the legislation passes, the Healthdyne board would be entrenched "well into 1998" and would be free to "frustrate the wishes of the rightful owners of Healthdyne," he said.
Invacare has said it intends to nominate seven candiates to replace the entire Healthdyne board at the yet-to-be-scheduled annual meeting.
